sheets.subject: ONLY an empty sky, nothing else in the picture: no land, no people, no animals. A hot dry clear midday sky, almost cloudless, two or three thin high wisps of cloud.
ONLY an empty sky, nothing else in the picture: no land, no people, no animals. A soft early morning sky with a few small cumulus clouds.
ONLY an empty sky, nothing else in the picture: no land, no people, no animals. A calm evening sky with long thin horizontal clouds.

Southern Levant, Natufian and early farming, c. 10,000-8,500 BCE (Ain Mallaha / Eynan in the Hula valley). Dry rolling limestone hills with scattered oak and terebinth trees and patches of wild grass, a far valley floor.

Lower Nile valley, Neolithic farmers, c. 5000-4500 BCE (Merimde Beni Salama and the Fayum). A broad calm Nile river across the strip, a narrow green band of reeds, acacias and small fields along the near and far bank, low red-brown desert cliffs beyond.

Lower Nile valley, Neolithic farmers, c. 5000-4500 BCE (Merimde Beni Salama and the Fayum). The Nile in its yearly flood: wide still water covering the fields, a few palms and acacias standing in the water, low desert cliffs beyond.
Southern Mesopotamia, Uruk period, c. 3400-3100 BCE, the city of Uruk and its irrigated plain. A wide slow Euphrates river on a completely flat plain, reed banks and groups of date palms along it.

Southern Mesopotamia, Uruk period, c. 3400-3100 BCE, the city of Uruk and its irrigated plain. The skyline of Uruk after archaeological reconstructions: many low flat-roofed mudbrick houses, and on the right a high whitewashed mudbrick platform with the White Temple of Anu on top (plain rectangular temple, buttressed walls).

Southern Mesopotamia, Uruk period, c. 3400-3100 BCE, the city of Uruk and its irrigated plain. A completely flat plain of irrigated barley fields divided by straight narrow canals with low earth banks, a few date palms, some fields cracked and dry.

items.reject: stepped ziggurat (Ur III, c. 2100 BCE) and a city wall: too late for Uruk

sheets.subject: Southern Levant, Natufian and early farming, c. 10,000-8,500 BCE (Ain Mallaha / Eynan in the Hula valley). (1) a round house partly sunk into the ground, low stone wall footing, conical roof of brushwood and hides on poles, as excavated at Ain Mallaha; (2) a small lean-to of branches covered with animal hides; (3) a small fire of sticks in a ring of stones with a thin column of smoke; (4) a dense stand of wild barley and wild wheat.

Lower Nile valley, Neolithic farmers, c. 5000-4500 BCE (Merimde Beni Salama and the Fayum). (1) a small oval hut of bundled reeds plastered with Nile mud, as at Merimde; (2) a small boat made of bundled papyrus reeds; (3) a patch of young green barley growing in black Nile mud; (4) a round grain storage pit in the ground lined with coiled basketry, as found in the Fayum.

Southern Mesopotamia, Uruk period, c. 3400-3100 BCE, the city of Uruk and its irrigated plain. (1) a short straight section of irrigation canal with water between low earth banks; (2) a canal being dug: a straight trench with heaps of dug earth beside it and a wooden hoe and a reed basket left on the bank; (3) a small earth dam of packed earth and reed bundles across a ditch; (4) a huge heap of harvested barley grain.

Southern Mesopotamia, Uruk period, c. 3400-3100 BCE, the city of Uruk and its irrigated plain. After archaeological reconstructions: (1) a cluster of three flat-roofed mudbrick houses with small doorways; (2) a potter's workshop: an open courtyard with a low turntable, unfired pots drying and a round domed kiln; (3) a horizontal ground loom pegged to the ground with a half-woven cloth; (4) a short section of mudbrick wall decorated with a clay cone mosaic in zigzag and diamond patterns, as in the Eanna precinct.

Near East, early farming. Animals side view, same scale: (1) an early domestic goat with long scimitar horns, (2) an early domestic hairy sheep with horns, (3) a mountain gazelle, (4) a small mixed herd of four sheep and goats.

Southern Levant, Natufian and early farming, c. 10,000-8,500 BCE (Ain Mallaha / Eynan in the Hula valley). Two rows of three, after real finds: (1) a curved bone sickle handle with a row of small flint blades set in it, (2) a basalt saddle quern with its handstone, (3) an open leather bag full of grain, (4) a broken round flat bread, (5) a fishing net with stone sinkers, (6) a Nile fish (tilapia).

Southern Mesopotamia, Uruk period, c. 3400-3100 BCE, the city of Uruk and its irrigated plain. Two rows of three, after finds from Uruk: (1) a coarse beveled-rim bowl, (2) a stack of beveled-rim bowls, (3) a small clay tablet with proto-cuneiform signs and number marks, (4) a few small clay tokens: cones, spheres and discs, (5) a woven reed basket, (6) a wooden hoe.

items.reject: grey metal-looking hoe blade: anachronism risk for Uruk farmers

sheets.subject: Near East river valleys, early farming. (1) a tall clump of papyrus reeds, (2) a date palm, (3) a clump of wild grass, (4) a clump of green barley, (5) a long cedar log lying on the ground.
Near East early farming: freshly sown field ground of dark moist earth in long shallow furrows with a few seedlings.
Near East dry country: a worn dirt path of pale dusty earth with tufts of dry wild grass at its edges.
Southern Mesopotamia: dry pale river silt baked by the sun, cracked into irregular plates, a few dry grass stalks.
Southern Mesopotamia, Uruk period: an irrigated barley field seen close, rows of young green barley in damp dark earth with a thin water furrow.
Southern Mesopotamia, Uruk period: a packed earth courtyard floor with a few broken mudbricks, straw and pottery sherds scattered sparsely.
Nile and Euphrates riverbank: damp grey-brown silt with footprints of birds, short reed stubs and small puddles.

Near East, early farming village (PPNA, c. 9000 BCE). (1) a round partly sunken hut: a low stone footing, a conical roof of reeds and brushwood, a small low doorway; (2) a small open cooking fire in a ring of stones with a thin line of smoke. Each object must read clearly when it is shown small, about a tenth of the screen height: one bold, closed, slightly broken outer contour, a simple silhouette, a few large inner shapes, and its own small patch of ground under it that ends in a few short strokes.

Near East river valleys and dry hills, early farming, c. 9000-3500 BCE. Small ground dressing pieces, six separate low objects in two rows: (1) a low tuft of dry wild grass, (2) a small spiny thorn shrub, (3) three pale sandstone stones together, (4) a low clump of young reeds, (5) a small tamarisk bush, (6) a clump of wild barley stalks.
Southern Mesopotamia, Uruk period, c. 3400 BCE: an irrigated barley field of young green barley in rows with a narrow muddy irrigation channel of water running across.
Southern Mesopotamia, Uruk period, c. 3400 BCE: a river bank of damp grey-brown silt with footprints, cracked drying mud and a few reed stubs.
Southern Mesopotamia, Uruk period, c. 3400 BCE: a packed earth courtyard with scattered broken mudbrick pieces, straw and potsherds, worn smooth by feet.

Near East river valleys and dry hills, early farming, c. 9000-3500 BCE. 6 flat ground patches in two rows: (1) a worn dusty footpath segment, (2) a darker patch of dry grass, (3) a scatter of small pale sandstone stones, (4) a patch of damp dark river mud with cracks, (5) a patch of trampled earth with straw, (6) a patch of broken mudbrick pieces and potsherds.
